# Partition Array by Equivalence Function

## Problem

You are provided with an integer array `nums` and a predefined **equivalence function** `equiv(x, y)`. This function returns `true` when `x` and `y` belong to the same equivalence class, and `false` otherwise. You may assume that `equiv` defines a proper equivalence relation—it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.

Your objective is to divide the elements of `nums` into a collection of subarrays according to the equivalence relation. The following rules must be respected:
- Every element inside a single subarray must be equivalent to every other element in that subarray.
- Any two elements taken from different subarrays must **not** be equivalent.
- The internal order of elements within each subarray must be identical to their original order in `nums`. The order in which the subarrays themselves appear in the result does not matter.

**Constraints:**
- 1 ≤ `nums.length` ≤ 10^4
- -10^9 ≤ `nums[i]` ≤ 10^9

**Example 1:**
> **Input:** nums = [2, 4, 7, 9, 6], equiv(x, y) => (x % 2 == y % 2)
> **Output:** [[2, 4, 6], [7, 9]]
> **Explanation:** The equivalence function groups numbers by their parity. The even numbers 2, 4, and 6 maintain their sequence in one subarray, while the odd numbers 7 and 9 form another.

**Example 2:**
> **Input:** nums = [5, 10, 15, 20], equiv(x, y) => (x % 5 == y % 5)
> **Output:** [[5, 10, 15, 20]]
> **Explanation:** Every element is divisible by 5 with no remainder, so all of them are equivalent and end up in a single group in their original order.

**Example 3:**
> **Input:** nums = [-1, 1, -2, 0, 5, -9, 0, 8], equiv(x, y) => (x and y have the same sign)
> **Output:** [[-1, -2, -9], [1, 5, 8], [0, 0]]
> **Explanation:** Equivalence is determined by having the same sign. Negative numbers, positive numbers, and zeros each form their own group, preserving their relative sequence within each group.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of the equivalence function as defining groups where you can check if two items belong together, but you don't know the group labels upfront.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a union-find (disjoint set union) data structure to efficiently merge elements that are equivalent and then collect the groups.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Aim for O(n^2) worst-case if you must call equiv for every pair, but optimize by only comparing each new element with one representative per group.

</details>
